display.title: Tanya Shiur 38: Chapter 27, Stray Thoughts and the Beinoni's Battle
display.summary_short: A Yiddish Tanya shiur opening chapter 27: why a beinoni should rejoice, not despair, each time he pushes away a stray thought, with talks on niggunim, the value of time and saying every word of davening clearly.
display.summary_long: Shiur 38 in Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish Tanya series begins with the proper time for bitterness: Krias Shema at bedtime, when the soul is entrusted to Hashem and returned each morning, which is why we say Modeh Ani with such gratitude. Digressions follow on the power of niggunim, including the Baal Shem Tov's promise about the niggun of his disciple Reb Michel of Zlotchov; on serving Hashem inwardly rather than for show, as in giving tzedakah in secret; and on the preciousness of time and why Hashem made us sleep, with teachings of the Frierdiker Rebbe on the soul's ascent at night. After reviewing chapter 26, the shiur opens chapter 27: a stray or improper thought is no cause for sadness. Pushing it away fulfils the mitzvah of 'do not stray after your heart and eyes', brings great pleasure Above and weakens the forces of evil. Being upset only shows that a person mistakes himself for a tzaddik. A beinoni may battle all his life, and this may be the very purpose he was created for. Further digressions urge saying every word of davening, Tehillim and benching clearly, and reciting the Twelve Pesukim. In this copy the recording is interrupted by a long silence about half an hour in.
display.lesson: A stray thought is no reason for sadness; each time a person pushes it away he does a mitzvah and gives Hashem great pleasure, so he should serve Him with joy.

study_text.note: Review of chapter 26, then the first part of chapter 27 (through the explanation of 'You created the wicked'). Same shiur as '38 cont P27'.

segments.title: A set time for bitterness: Shema at bedtime
segments.summary: The soul is entrusted to Hashem at night and returned each morning, which is why we thank Him in Modeh Ani and ask forgiveness before sleep.

segments.title: The power of a niggun
segments.summary: Niggunim express every feeling in serving Hashem, and the Baal Shem Tov promised to plead for whoever sings Reb Michel of Zlotchov's niggun with true teshuvah.

segments.title: Serving Hashem inwardly, not for show
segments.summary: Chassidus asks that a mitzvah be done sincerely and quietly, like tzedakah given in secret.

segments.title: The value of time and the purpose of sleep
segments.summary: Time cannot be controlled, only filled; sleep is no waste, because a soul that served Hashem by day ascends and learns Torah at night.

segments.title: Review of chapter 26: two kinds of sadness
segments.summary: Sadness that leads to despair is forbidden; bitterness that leads to change is part of serving Hashem.

segments.title: Tanya 27: stray thoughts and the beinoni
segments.summary: A stray thought is no cause for sadness; pushing it away fulfils the mitzvah of not straying after one's heart and eyes.

segments.title: Long silence
segments.summary: About 55 minutes with no speech; the shiur resumes exactly where it stopped.

segments.title: Tanya 27 continued: the beinoni's lifelong battle
segments.summary: Pushing away a stray thought brings pleasure Above; being upset by it is a sign of self-deception, and a beinoni may battle all his life.

segments.title: A mind without a roof
segments.summary: As one may not daven in a place without a roof, an empty mind invites stray thoughts, so keep it busy with a pasuk or Tehillim.

segments.title: Saying every word clearly
segments.summary: The yetzer hara pushes us to rush the words of davening, Tehillim and benching, though each word is precious; better to say less, clearly, from a siddur.

segments.title: Iskafya and the Twelve Pesukim
segments.summary: Know your place in serving Hashem, and when the yetzer hara knocks, do not let it in; recite the Twelve Pesukim, which are for adults too.

segments.title: Silence at the end
segments.summary: No speech for the last eight minutes of the file.
